narrative.title: Consolidating the Customer Identity Cards
narrative.scenario: A bank's onboarding system holds identity cards, each listing a name plus that card's email addresses. Cards belong to the same customer whenever they share even one email; shared names prove nothing. Compliance wants one consolidated card per customer — name first, then every distinct email sorted — regardless of how many raw cards fed it.
narrative.inputFormat: A list accounts where accounts[i] is [name, email1, email2, ...].
narrative.outputFormat: Return the merged accounts: each begins with the name followed by that person's emails in sorted order; the list order itself is free.
constraints: An email appears in at most one initial card's list more than once; names may repeat

complexity.optimalTime: O(N * M α(N) + E log E)

testCases.explanation: The first and third John cards share an email and merge; the second John stays separate despite the name.
A shared middle email chains the two Gabe cards into one sorted identity.

hintLevels: Level 1: Emails are the true identity keys — names are decoration.
Level 2: Map each email to a card index; any email seen under two cards unions those cards.
Level 3: Regroup emails by each card's union-find root, sort each group, and re-attach the name.
